queries: WITH c AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), t AS (SELECT SUM(n) AS total, AVG(n * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT c.sex, c.n AS test_records, c.n * 1.0 / t.total AS share_of_total, c.n - t.avg_n AS above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN t WHERE c.n > t.avg_n

WITH c AS (SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), t AS (SELECT SUM(n) * 1.0 AS total, AVG(n * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT c.SEX, c.n AS test_records, c.n * 1.0 / t.total AS share_of_total, c.n - t.avg_n AS above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN t WHERE c.n > t.avg_n ORDER BY c.n DESC

responses.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), t AS (SELECT SUM(n) AS total, AVG(n * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT c.sex, c.n AS test_records, c.n * 1.0 / t.total AS share_of_total, c.n - t.avg_n AS above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN t WHERE c.n > t.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: Only lab records whose ID matches a Patient row are counted (inner join). The average per sex is the matched record total divided by the number of sex groups that appear in those records.
'How far above the average' means the absolute difference in records (count minus average), not a percentage. The share of total is a fraction from 0 to 1. Neither is rounded.
If any matched patients have a NULL SEX, they form their own group and count toward the number of groups in the average.

assumptions.assumption: The average per sex is total matched lab records divided by the number of distinct SEX groups present in the matched data. A NULL SEX, if any, counts as its own group.
'How far above the average' is the absolute difference (count minus average), not a ratio or percentage. The share of total is a fraction from 0 to 1. Neither is rounded.
Only Laboratory rows whose ID matches a Patient row are counted (inner join).

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude patients with NULL or empty SEX, so the average is taken only over recorded sexes and the total excludes unknown-sex records.

assumptions.assumption: Lab records that match a patient means an inner join of Laboratory to Patient on ID. Lab rows with no matching patient are excluded.
The average per sex is total matched records divided by the number of distinct sex values present. Patients with NULL SEX are excluded, so NULL is not counted as a sex group.
Share of total is the sex's record count divided by the total across the listed sexes. How far above average is the count minus the average, as an absolute count and unrounded.
